topic: Dot Products and Duality: The Geometry of Interaction

outline.topic: Dot Products and Duality: The Geometry of Interaction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Projection Intuition
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as arrows. Introduce the dot product as the product of the length of one vector and the shadow (projection) cast by the other vector onto it. This transforms a 2D interaction into a 1D scalar value.
sections.example: Visualize a flashlight shining on a needle (vector v) resting on a table (vector w). The shadow length on the table represents the dot product.

sections.title: Defining Duality: The Linear Functional
sections.content: Explain that a dot product with a fixed vector 'w' is a machine that takes an input vector 'v' and outputs a scalar. This 'machine' is a linear functional. Duality states that every linear transformation from vectors to scalars is just a dot product in disguise.
sections.example: Think of 'w' as a 'filter' or 'gatekeeper'. If 'w' is a weight vector, the dot product calculates the 'total score' of a set of features (vector 'v').

sections.title: Visualizing the Dual Space
sections.content: Instead of arrows, represent the dot product result as a set of parallel lines (level sets). The vector 'w' defines the direction of the lines, and the dot product tells us which 'line' the input 'v' lands on.
sections.example: Use a topographic map: the vector 'w' points uphill, and the contour lines represent constant dot product values. Any vector 'v' landing on the same contour line has the same dot product with 'w'.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Power of Perspective
sections.content: Conclude by showing how duality allows us to bridge geometry (the vector) and algebra (the functional). Emphasize that the dot product is the bridge that turns geometry into calculation.
sections.example: A robotic arm (vector 'v') sensing a pressure field (defined by 'w'). The dot product calculates the total torque applied to the joint, showing how geometry informs physics.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Projection Intuition
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows representing direction and magnitude.
Dot product projects one vector onto another.
The shadow length measures the projection magnitude.
The dot product captures their geometric alignment.
animations: Draw projection line onto subspace S in #33FF57.
Rotate subspace S to show perspective shift.
Fade out all elements after concept summary.

storyboard.title: Defining Duality: The Linear Functional
lecture_lines: A fixed vector defines a linear functional.
It maps input vectors to scalar outputs.
This machine acts as a weight filter.
animations: Display linear functional f as a scalar map.
Visualize f acting on vector v as scalar.
Show f mapping vectors to lines #FF33A8.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Dual Space
lecture_lines: Visualize dot product results as level sets.
These are parallel lines perpendicular to w.
Vectors on the same line share dot products.
animations: Show space V and dual space V* as #F3FF33.
Animate duality pairing between V and V*.
Highlight isomorphism mapping between V and V*.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: The Power of Perspective
lecture_lines: Duality bridges geometry and algebraic calculation.
The dot product connects spatial properties.
It turns geometric intuition into powerful algebra.
animations: Display duality relationship in system equation form.
Overlay duality mapping onto original projection model.
Final summary with combined concepts in #FFFFFF.
